title: Refit a bakery mixer beater and verify a guarded start and stop
instruction: Fit the clean flat beater to the stopped bakery mixer: align its slotted hub, push it onto the shaft against the spring-loaded collar, turn it into the retaining pocket and release it. Seat the guard on the lowered bowl, raise the bowl with the lift handle, then run the mixer at its preset low speed for at least five seconds and switch it off. Leave both hands clear, the beater secured and the guard fitted.
context: Refitting mixer tools after cleaning and between batches is routine bakery equipment preparation. This task requires precise tool assembly followed by a guarded start-and-stop check.
setup: One fixed generic compact bench mixer: painted steel chassis with a 310 x 280 mm base, approximately 475 mm high; stainless bowl 232 mm across its outer rim and 142 mm deep, already mounted and clamped, empty and lowered. Painted steel external lift cradle: 18 x 255 x 18 mm rear bar, two 130 x 20 x 12 mm side arms and 20 x 20 x 25 mm trunnion risers. One 250 g aluminium flat beater, 109 mm wide and 195 mm high, with a 12.7 mm hub bore around a 12 mm shaft and a 4 mm drive pin. A 20 g stainless retaining collar (32 mm outside diameter, 18 mm bore, 1.5 mm thick) has 8 mm axial travel and a native spring with 5 N preload, 400 N/m stiffness and 4 N s/m damping. One 180 g stainless wire guard, approximately 235 x 261 x 62 mm including its polymer grip tab, supported 28 mm above the guard rim. Polymer draining supports: beater base 130 x 130 x 15 mm with retaining rails, and guard platform 260 x 250 x 20 mm. Manual lift handle with a rubber knob, 75 mm bowl travel; green START and red STOP polymer buttons, 4 mm travel. Wooden work surface 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm, top at 747.5 mm. Mixer base origin (350, 30, 747.5) mm; beater hub initially (240, 320, 987) mm before settling; guard rim origin (450, 310, 782.5) mm before settling. All initial orientations are identity. Both robot hands start open in READY. Robot bases: (0, +/-305, 750) mm. Coordinates: x forward, y left, z up. geometry.json gives all colliders; setup.png shows the settled layout.
scoring: Numeric rubric: 0.25 after one second of released beater retention: hub radial error <0.5 mm, height error <0.6 mm about 6 mm below the shaft pin, tilt <3 degrees and relative yaw within 10 degrees of -60 degrees. Native contact checks must show no beater contact except the shaft and its spring collar; propping with the guard or fingers earns no retention credit. Both gripper centres must be >75 mm from the hub centre and centreline points 40, 105 and 170 mm below it. 0.50 additionally requires guard centre error <3 mm, height error <1.5 mm about 144.5 mm above the bowl origin, tilt <2 degrees, yaw <5 degrees and both gripper centres >190 mm from the guard centre for one second. 0.75 additionally requires bowl lift within 1.5 mm of 75 mm. 1.00 requires five consecutive seconds with these physical assembly conditions, clear hands, motor enabled, beater and shaft each 136 +/-8 rpm clockwise and carrier 60 +/-5 rpm counterclockwise; then a STOP press >=3 mm and a two-second endpoint with all rotations <1 rpm, motor off, buttons released below 1 mm travel, assembly retained and hands clear. Disassembly invalidates an earlier run. Otherwise award only the attained partial stage, or zero if none. A beater/guard origin outside x=(-180,900) mm, y=[-650,650] mm, z=[727.5,1500] mm latches zero. During powered or subsequent coasting rotation >5 rpm, a gripper centre inside the bowl-centred 145 mm radius and between 20 mm below the bowl origin and world z=1097.5 mm, or guard/bowl disengagement, latches zero. All tolerance limits are strict unless an inclusive inequality or closed interval is explicitly shown; a value exactly at a strict limit fails that condition.
reset_notes: No consumables. Stop the apparatus, lower and empty the bowl, and return the guard and beater to their supports. Reset motor, button and scoring state. In simulation, recreate and settle the fixed scene before beginning the control budget.
fidelity: Generic rigid Isaac Sim/PhysX model at 960 Hz. Physical pin/L-slot contacts, a passive spring collar, wire guard and linked lift; masses and inertias are lumped approximations. Independently regulated torque-limited orbit/spin drives use an assumed ratio and 2 s soft start/stop. Internal gearing, food, deformation and electrical faults are omitted. Interlock loss brakes immediately. Hand-clearance checks are operational proxies, not certified injury thresholds.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (3,600 controls); scripted demo: 1.0 (3,540 controls).
